2026-11-23.title: Monday of the Thirty-fourth Week in Ordinary Time
readings: They follow the Lamb wherever he goes
Lord, this is the people that longs to see your face
The poor widow put in more than all of them
2026-11-23.alt: Optional memorials: St Clement I, pope and martyr; St Columban, abbot; Bl. Miguel Agustín Pro, priest and martyr.
2026-11-23.verse: He said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all of them; for all of them have contributed out of their abundance, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.”
theo: In the last week of the year the Gospel turns to Jesus' final teaching in the Temple. He watches people putting gifts into the treasury. The rich give large sums; a poor widow puts in two small copper coins. Jesus says she has given more than all, because they gave from their surplus and she gave “all she had to live on”. God measures a gift not by its size but by the love and trust it carries.

In Revelation John sees the Lamb standing on Mount Zion with the 144,000 who bear his name and his Father's name on their foreheads; “these follow the Lamb wherever he goes”. The widow is one of them: she follows the Lamb who will soon give not two coins but his whole life. Total self-giving is the mark of those who belong to him.
outline: Ask: if Jesus sat by the collection box today, what would he say about your offering?
His followers bear his name and go where he goes.
live: Give something today that costs you, not only from surplus.
Make the Sign of the Cross slowly and deliberately each time you pray today.
2026-11-23.prayer: Lord Jesus, you saw the widow's two coins and praised her love. Teach me to give not only from my surplus but from my heart, and to follow you, the Lamb, wherever you go. Amen.

quick: God measures gifts by love, not amount.
The widow gave all she had.
Those who belong to the Lamb follow him wherever he goes.
2026-11-23.action: Give something today that really costs you.
2026-11-23.question: Do I give God my surplus or my heart?

homily: Dear friends, in this last week of the Church's year, Jesus sits near the Temple treasury and watches people putting in their gifts. The rich put in large sums; a poor widow puts in two small copper coins. Jesus says she has put in more than all of them, for they gave out of their abundance, but she out of her poverty gave all she had to live on (Luke 21:3–4).
God does not measure a gift by its size, but by the love and trust it carries. The widow trusted God with her whole living. That is why her two coins outweigh all the gold.

In Revelation John sees the Lamb standing on Mount Zion with those who bear his name and his Father's name on their foreheads; they follow the Lamb wherever he goes (Revelation 14:1, 4). The widow belongs to them: she follows the Lamb who will soon give not two coins but his whole life.
Let us ask ourselves honestly: do I give God what is left over, or do I give him my heart? Today, give something that truly costs you, in money, in time or in patience, and give it with joy. Amen.
kids: Children, the poor widow gave only two little coins, but Jesus said she gave the most, because she gave with all her heart. Give Jesus your best today!

intro: Those who follow the Lamb give themselves wholly, as the widow did.

sub: The Lamb stands on Mount Zion.
q: Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD? And who shall stand in his holy place? Those who have clean hands and pure hearts, who do not lift up their souls to what is false, and do not swear deceitfully.
Then I looked, and there was the Lamb, standing on Mount Zion! And with him were one hundred forty-four thousand who had his name and his Father's name written on their foreheads.
points.apply: Make the Sign of the Cross with attention today.

q: She went and did as Elijah said, so that she as well as he and her household ate for many days. The jar of meal was not emptied, neither did the jug of oil fail, according to the word of the LORD that he spoke by Elijah.
He said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all of them; for all of them have contributed out of their abundance, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.”
For the LORD does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
points.apply: Review your giving this year honestly.

concl: Small gifts given wholly are great before God.
Follow the Lamb who gave everything.
2026-11-23.resolve: Decide on your Advent and Christmas giving to the poor now.
